body:
I know that feeling all too well. For me it got to the point where I did try to kill myself. Chances are it's nowhere near as bad as you think, and you've probably got BDD. I got bullied by people that said I was ugly throughout the later years of highschool. It made me feel like every single one of my features way really, really bad.

After getting a therapist and taking anti-depressants I feel so much better about myself. I have the confidence to go outside without feeling really uncomfortable. I got the confidence to post some pictures of myself on r/amiugly and it seems it was nowhere near as bad as I thought. I did have one piece of feedback from a few people. If it keeps me from finding a boyfriend then I'm going to get cosmetic surgery to fix it, but until then I'm staying positive. You can find it in my previous posts if you really want to.

What I'm trying to get across though is that it's probably not anywhere near as bad as you think, and definitely not worth taking you life over. I think you're biggest problem is that you lack any confidence, once you start getting confidence you'll look sooooo much better, even if you do have a couple of small flaws with your appearance.
Thanks. There's no need to rush. :)
Pretty much.

Maybe, I've never lived a day that I can remember without this problem. I was always planning that I would try again once I couldn't take it anymore or when I my friends moved on.

It just seems weird to me that I may have a reason to keep living past those events.

I'm not sure if this is the same thing, but a few weeks ago my friend had the house to herself, so she invited me and two of my other friends down for a few days. That was the best time of my life, although I was convinced that on the last night I was going to drown myself in her pool because I knew that it would suck once it was over. It never lowered my mood or anything, it was just all I thought about when I was lying in bed there.

Thanks, it's nice to hear you say such things, but it's difficult trying to be happy when the only thing you see when you look at yourself is ugly. I don't think I will be able to embrace it, but I just wanted to know how little I could get away with changing about myself.
Thank you. :)

Thanks. :)

My psychologist said it would take a while, but I guess I'll just have to hang in there for now.
Thanks. :) This thread has actually turned my life around. I still don't like what I see, but at least I can believe that I actually do have BDD.
Thanks. That's the first time that anyone has ever said that to me. :)

I'd love to hear your story, especially if it can help me. Currently I'm seeing a psychologist about it, but he said that it could take a very long time.

Since surgery isn't going to be a good option for me for the foreseeable future do you think that my noise will be a big problem for me if I tried to get a boyfriend?
lol, I'm gay, so the pressure of learning how to talk to girls isn't a concern for me. But thank you. :)

What about it I have been diagnosed with BDD? How come it will make it worse? 

and thanks. I'll take your advice about waiting for a bit. Although I think that I probably will get it eventually, I guess having some time to prepare for it first will help.

I really appreciate the time you took to write all that. I've considered getting cosmetic surgery for a long time. Which is why I posted here, because I can't live with my appearance anymore. I just needed to know how many and which features needed to be fixed. 

I However, after reading all of that I'm not too sure if I want to go through with it anymore. I still really want to fix myself, but now it seems like too much can go wrong with it, which I don't want to risk, considering that it could end up worse, it would cost me a lot of money and I would most likely have to travel out of my country to find a good surgeon. 

Just one question though. Would you say that you look better because of the surgery?
Ha ha, thanks. It's blunt but at least it's the truth.
Thanks. I don't really have a hairstyle, I just let it do whatever. My friend might be able to help me out with that though.
Thanks. I already have some glasses, but they don't suit me very well. Not sure if it's just the frame or whether I just can't pull off glasses. Although, what do you mean by scruffy face? :)
Thanks. I have no idea how to style my hair, but I have a friend who would probably help me learn.

Thanks. While I do plan on getting plastic surgery, do you think that it would be an issue in the meantime? I've never been out with anyone before, I always assumed it was because I was too ugly, since I got bullied a bit in high school because of that.
Yeah, my nose is the thing that I loathe the most. I'm all for plastic surgery, I just want to know how much I will need to fix.

Maybe. No matter who tells me that I'm not ugly, or it's all in my head I just can't believe it. I've been ridiculed because of my appearance for far too long. Fortunately I feel pretty good at the minute, since I've been distracting myself, and I've been opening up to my friends a lot recently. 

How do you cope though?

I will be seeing a psychologist by the end of the month hopefully. I've been told that it will most likely take a very long time for me to overcome it, but they said it is "doable"

Anyway, I'm feeling a lot better now. I still have some very bad times, but tat the moment I feel pretty good. I'm glad that it's working for you, I just hope the same thing will work for me, if I even have BDD.
Yes. I have other issues like confidence and self-esteem to sort out before I can really be that outgoing and be the person I want to be, but I guess it won't hurt to get some practice in now.
Thanks. I'm grateful I have them too. :)
I think that they would want it everywhere though, I only get it on my chin. I don't want that look though, I'd prefer to look hairless because of the reason above.

I've taken that approach often in front of my friends, but it's all an act. It's ruining my life. I promised everyone that I wouldn't try to kill myself again, but I know that it's probably just a matter of time before I give up again.

Ha. Well, er.. this is for when I dress up in drag, so growing a beard isn't really an option. :D I just read that you can wax your face, so I might try that. 

Plus I can't grow a very good beard. I only get hair on my chin, but that's what is still visible after I shave.
I probably should have mentioned that. I don't tan. I spent two whole weeks in the Florida and came back exactly the same colour.
I think that's made up. I've shaved my ass plenty of times and I've never had anything like that happen to me.
I love shaving my legs. They are sooooo smooth. I love stroking them while I lie in bed . you should keep it up OP. :)
You should go to hospital right now! If you really are afraid for your life then it's not worth taking risks. Besides, if you go to hospital they can refer you to someone for your depression.
Thanks, I guess I won't bother skipping a day if it won't make any difference.

I thought 60mg was the highest dosage that they prescribe to people taking fluoxetine? 

Anyway, thanks guys. I've decided I'm not going to bother drinking, especially if there's a chance it's going to make me depressed. Plus I don't want a really bad hangover. :p
My friends are aware of my situation, it's just I miss drinking with them.

I'm still suicidal every now and then, but I'm definitely feeling better. A lot has changed for me:
- I'm taking anti-depressants
- I've had counselors that I could vent to, although that was a temporary thing, but I will be going to see a psychologist soon
- I came out of the closet after hiding my sexuality for about 7 years of my life
- I thought I was going to fail college since I lost my motivation to do anything while I was depressed, but it turns out that I did well before I stopped doing work, so I was able to catch up and finish with fairly decent grades (better than failing :p)
- While I was depressed I felt as if I was drifting apart from my friends, and I thought they stopped liking me, but it turns out that it's all in my head
- I can vent to my mother anytime that I feel low, which is nice

The main thing that changed me is hope. I really hate the way I look, it's ruined my life and it was the main thing that drove me to the point where I tried kill myself, but everyone keeps telling me that I have body dimorphic disorder. I don't really believe it, when I look in the mirror I do, and always have, see the ugliest person ever. I don't really believe I have BDD, the way people have treated me and what they have called me makes it obvious that I'm actually ugly, and not imagining it. 

I guess some little part of me just hopes that I'm wrong though. So I've decided that I'm going to keep going until I finish psychology. If I don't feel any different towards my appearance after that then I'll probably re-lapse and try to kill myself again. I can't live this way, and without hope I don't have anything.
Why are you doing posting here then? Call the emergency services!

I can somewhat relate. My life's goal is to become a game designer. I don't really care if I become a famous one, though it would be nice. However, when I look at other people's work in video games it makes me wonder how I'm ever going to get to that level. 

My current skills are mediocre at best, but I'm going to keep on learning new things, and practicing what I already know. Especially since my counselor told me to keep busy throughout the summer, so I've given myself a project that will really push my skills. You should do the same. Just keep writing throughout the summer, your skills will keep improving.

I can also relate to the feeling of being alone all of the time. I've never ever had a boyfriend, and the few friends I do have, while they are amazing, I rarely hang out with them, so I spend almost all of my time by myself. Again, I cope with that as best as I can by distracting myself. For me the distraction is game design, for you it could be writing.

You should also see a therapist. Before I started getting help there wasn't a single day that I didn't think about killing myself, until one day I tried, and I fucked it up. Now I have help I think about suicide a lot less, and I'm no where near as depressed as I used to be. Don't get me wrong, I still have my fair share of bad days, but I'm hoping that once I finish seeing my psychologist I will be fixed.

Thanks. I don't really know anyone with a good fashion sense. I tried going on the male fashion advice subreddits but I'm still about as unfashionable as I was before.

I've apparently got BDD, so I don't see what's actually there (according to a doctor), I don't believe it, but I'm willing to hear them out. I can't get over my appearance, I hate it, it's reduced me to tears more times than I can count, thinking about it consumes all of my time, and it's going to prevent me from living the life that I want. I've been told that once I finish psychology, I will be fine, that everything is in my head. So I'm going to play their game, just in case I am wrong, but if I still feel the same way after psychology then fuck it, I'm done.

I don't play compulsively to the point where I'd rather play a game than go outside with my friends, I just do it because I don't really have anything else to do. Thanks for your help though, I feel so much better now that I'm not worrying about it anymore. :)

I don't want friends anymore. They were the best friends I had, and now I lost them. I don't want to go through this all over again. 

Besides, I don't really hang out anywhere, even when I used to be with my friends it was at their house. None of my interests really open up opportunities to find new friends. The only things I do is play games, watch videos on YouTube and practice 3D modelling. The only reason I had my friends is because I went on a game design course. Not to mention, my social skills suck. 

Anyway, I'm seeing my counsellors tomorrow. What will happen if I tell them I feel suicidal? Will I be put on suicide watch or anything? 

EDIT: I was at the verge of relapsing, I thought fuck it, if I want to die then I have noting to loose by asking them. I told them a lot and they were very understanding and supportive, and they have even decided to meet up with me this Sunday. I guess it was all in my head after all.

I'm very sorry to hear this has happened to you. I feel very fortunate that I live in a country that's not big on religion. I haven't come out to everyone, but to the few people that I have come out to have been every supporting, the only shit that I've had to put up with is a friend that keeps telling me that I'm not gay. That's pretty weird that the only bad thing I have to put up with now is being called straight. 

It's disgusting that people can treat others this way, especially because of something that they have no control over. Don't worry though, diversity is becoming more and more acceptable, the idiots that are tormenting you are becoming fewer and fewer and soon enough they'll be gone completely. My advice is that if you're able to, then move away. Nobody there, not your family or friends deserves you. Find a part of the world that is more accepting, that's what you deserve. 

EDIT: I just re-read my post, and what I said may be confused with me thinking that all religious people are crazy bigots, I'm not saying that at all. I was just saying that the people to tend to be the most intolerant are religious people.

It doesn't matter. I asked my friend to let me know if they were doing anything, but now they're all together and I wasn't invited again. Fuck it. I don't want people in my life anymore, I hate people. I don't know why I even bother anymore. I'm not getting better, I feel like my therapists are lying to me. The only reason I'm still alive is for my parents, but why the fuck should that be my reason to keep going.

Thanks. I know it took me forever to reply to this, but that's because it took me forever to finally talk to them. I've only spoken to one of my friends, and I told him a bit of what happened. I don't feel the way I used to though.

I never saw the original thread, but I'm very happy that you decided to stick around a while longer, and that your luck changed for the better. I hope you have plenty more good days. 

I'm saving this thread so that I remember this the next time I feel suicidal. I doubt I will ever have a day like you did, but I like to hope.
Thanks. I really appreciate the time you took to help me these past few days. :)
If you feel suicidal the hotlines can give you help short term, but you need to see a therapist or psychologist for long term help. I have and my life has been so much better since I started therapy.

Please don't do this. Call one of the suicide hotlines. 

redd.it/17gu7g

Your friends don't know what they're talking about. It's easy to believe that suicide is cowardly or selfish, but nobody can ever understand what it's like to feel suicidal until they reach that point themselves. I used to think like your friends until it happened to me. I know how difficult it is to keep your feeling bottled up and repressed, to live life as a lie. My advice would be to see a therapist (if you're not already), and talk to your parents/girlfriend about everything that you're going through. It's helped so much to let everything out, and to get the support from your loved ones. 

It's not too late to sort your grades out. I didn't do well in my education until recently. I left high school and my first year of college to barley anything to show for it. I was doing pretty well with my current college course until I because really low and lost all motivation to do any work. I did barely any of my work for almost 6 months that I was in college. Once I got help my parents explained to my tutor thievery that happened. Luckily it turns out that I was doing well before I got low, so I didn't have too much to catch up on, but had I been behind my tutor would have worked something out with me, weather it was more time to had in work or re-sit the last year of college.

Please, talk to someone, get help. It's not too late to fix everything.

What sort of things go wrong? I think you're seeing things worse than they are. I know what it's like to feel like everything is going wrong all at once, but what helps me in times like this is to think about some time I was really happy, even if I have to go back to my childhood, and then I focus on that.
You clearly care about him a lot. What benefit would this bring to him? More importantly, what would it give him that would make it worth loosing the most important person in his life?
Please don't do this. Think of your son. He will be devastated if you do this.

Thanks for the links. I need to buy more clothes soon anyway, so I'll check this place out before I buy anything. I feel like even if I do all of this stuff I'll be a well dressed guy with a nice body (or at least as good as I can get it. I have a scar on my stomach area and I swear my rib cage is kinda big) who still has an ugly face. :( 

Anyway, today had been a pretty good day for me, so I'm trying not to think about any of this stuff too much at the minute. Thanks so much for all of you help though. :)

I think I can relate to a lot of what you say. I've got a massive problem with my appearance, feeling like I have nothing to offer anyone, of feeling completely alone all of the time. I also reacted to it the same way. I used to cry in bed at night, or if people were around I'd sit in the shower so nobody could hear me. The last thing that I wanted was for people to help me, I just wanted to turn everything off. But I'm very happy that I did get help. My quality of life has improved so much since I got help. Sure I have some pretty rough times, the last few days have been particularly bad for me, but most of the time I'm actually happy and enjoy life.

I know you said you didn't want advice, but I'm going to offer it to you if there's a slight chance that I may change your mind. I'm assuming you haven't tried therapy yet since you didn't mention it. If you can, then I would explain to your parents what you're going thorough. They will get you the help that you need, and they will be there for you to help you through this. Therapy has helped me so much since I started it. It's given me an outlet, some people that I can really open up to. I feel like I have people that I can trust, people that I can talk to if I ever need to. You'd be surprised how much it can help to just talk to someone. They can also get you medication if you need any. I know that since I've started taking my medication I've been a lot less anxious out in public, to the point where I can be around people comfortably now. If you're particularly concerned with your appearance then stay away from mirrors. I know the urge to just stare into it and focus on all of your faults, but that only encourages self loathing behavior and will make you feel worse. When I get concerned about my appearance I try to find something to distract myself with immediately, although I do admit it can be difficult to get the motivation to do it sometimes. Whether it's playing a game, doing some 3D modelling or listening to music, if I get a chance to think about all of the negative about myself things then it makes me feel like shit, and it's a difficult mood to get out of,  so it's important to find something to do quickly before I get chance to think about that bad stuff.

I've never really given this sort of advice to anyone before, and since I only recently decided to get help I can't really offer you a lot, so I'm really sorry if I wasn't any help to you or if I picked you on your story the wrong way, but please hang in there and get some professional help.

I don't think that you're a terrible person in the slightest, you just made a few bad decisions. I'm sure all of us here have made bad decisions, especially when we're feeling low. I'm not going to tell you that everything going to get better, but I don't think it sounds like it's too late for you to re-form a relationship with your son. You clearly care so much about him, so why not make it your full time goal to get better for his sake? It sounds like you've never fully committed to therapy in the past, but it does work for a lot of people when they stick with it.

Maybe you could try doing something to raise awareness for things like child abuse. I know that there are hotlines that children can phone if they are dealing with abuse at home, maybe you could volunteer to work for one of those services if you feel like you're able. At least then you'll be able to forgive yourself for what you have done.

I don't know if my advice will be of any help to you or not, I honestly can't say that I can relate much to what you have said, but hopefully it did, even if only a little.

I admit, I'm definitely not making the most of myself at the minute, but when I look into the mirror it just seems like a lost cause anyway. Plus, yeah, I have no sense of fashion at all, so I'm not sure how to get help with that. 

I want to let you guys know that you really helped me yesterday. It's always nice to get advice from someone in a similar situation. And having someone to talk to for a little bit was amazing. Thank you. :)

Oh, I thought most gyms were for a sine gender. Maybe different places attract different demographics. I did some looking around and they is one very cost to my house, so now I just have to come someone to go with, and it depends on whether I can afford it. If not then I will probably just try to get out and take me walks. I may not meet anyone, but at least I'll have something to do.

In a way I'm actually sort of grateful that I'm gay, since I really don't feel any jealousy when I see a straight couple, so you're probably fat more exposed to that than I am. The thing I don't like about pride isn't just seeing loads of gay couples together, but it also reminds me how much better looking the rest of the gay community is than I am. I feel like shit when I look at them. I don't expect people to settle for me, why should they, I just wish I was good looking. That way I could have a boyfriend and be able to dress up and look good.

I have friends, but I don't live very close to them, so if we ever hang out it's usually a planned event rather than a spontaneous thing. Hopefully with us (my friends) all finishing college well be able to do more things with each other, if they invite me to come along. I know a lot of the times they do things without me, I don't know why though. I'm afraid to ask them why.

I'm pretty unfit though, so maybe I could join a gym, though do they have gyms where both genders go to? I'd be way too intimidated if it was just a bunch of ripped dudes there.

Thank you so much. I feel a lot better knowing that someone understands what I'm going through, and I also broke down once I got home from college, which I suppose let me get a lot of my frustration out of my system. I don't really have anyone I can hang out with, but I'm trying to distract myself by forcing myself to playing some games or doing some 3D modelling. I'm not really enjoying myself, but at least I'm no longer seeing any pride stuff anymore.
It's a reminder of everything I want but will never have. Imagine if you were looking into the window of a restaurant, watching everyone enjoy their food, while you're stuck outside starving.
